glosses: Curved or bowed outward like the outside of a bowl, circle, or sphere.

examples.text: [D]rops of water naturally form themselves into figures with a convex surface; […]

glosses: having an epigraph that is a convex set.
having no internal angles greater than 180 degrees.
arranged such that for any two points in the set, a straight line between the two points is contained within the set.
Any convex body or surface.

examples.text: Half heaven's convex glitters with the flame.

glosses: A playing card made convex for use in cheating.
A small convex mirror used to cheat by observing other players' cards.

examples.text: Of all the devices for defrauding at poker, the “shiner,” or “convex” […] Modern convexes are also considerably larger than those of former days.

glosses: To form a convex curve or surface; to become convex.

examples.text: In like manner the north pier will convex seaward, extending across the bay to the extent of 1000 feet from low water, terminating in about eight fathoms, leaving a clear entrance of 500 feet between the pier heads, the depth of the entrance being from seven to eight fathoms.
If the valve is ground excessively, the surfaces of the valve and cage will convex so that the sealing contact is poor.
With thin metal flashing, as it expands, the metal between the fasteners will convex.

glosses: To cause to form a convex curve or surface; to make convex.

examples.text: The back edge of the saw being under the lip of the cleat, use the anvil for a fulcrum and press down on the edge of the saw opposite, which will convex the plate, as the springing up concaved it, and the action of the fast and loose will be the reverse; that is, the fast will go down and the loose come up.
This will convex the fan and hold the cards more rigidly in place.
In one moment the body will convex the checkered blanket, and later—the featureless absence;

glosses: To circulate or cause to circulate in a curved path; to cause or exhibit convection.

examples.text: The crystal/melt interface thus convexes into the melt; however, the convexity of the interface ( Figure 53 ) is not as strong as it is when the crucible does not rotate (Figure 52).
The lid on will convex the heat and you'll need that after it's been chilled.

translations.source_sense_description: Physik, Optik: nach außen gewölbt, allgemein: vom Betrachter aus gesehen zu ihm hin gewölbt

glosses: Qui présente une surface bombée.

examples.text: Un miroir, un verre convexe.

Pour le dessert, Jeanine avait prévu un vin de Cilaos avec le gâteau. Mémé Gâté, grande amatrice de ce breuvage moelleux, avait exigé qu’on en remplisse son verre à ras bord. C’est-à-dire jusqu’à ce que le précieux liquide forme un débord convexe au-dessus de son verre.

glosses: Qui présente une courbe en bosse.

examples.text: Le lit de la Lanterne dans la vallée moyenne, celui du Breuchin […] et de la Semouse dans leur section inférieure sont envahis sur la rive convexe par des bancs de cailloutis exondés aux basses eaux […]
Ligne courbe convexe. — Un cercle, une ellipse sont convexes.

glosses: Qualifie une surface qui ne peut être rencontrée par une ligne droite en plus de deux points.
Qualifie un polygone plan dont les sommets sont dans un même demi-plan par rapport à n’importe quel côté du polygone.
Qui contient tout segment reliant deux de ses points.

examples.text: Tout disque est convexe.

glosses: Dont la courbe représentative délimite une partie supérieure convexe (c’est-à-dire que tout segment reliant deux points de la courbe représentative est « au-dessus » de la courbe).

examples.text: La fonction carré est convexe, de même que la fonction exponentielle.

glosses: Ensemble convexe.

examples.text: L’intersection de deux convexes est elle-même convexe.
